text: With a validated load behind you, fact_orders is now the trustworthy, repeatable source Finance's report will run on. But primary path doesn't mean only path. Every row in fact_orders went through a full COPY — worth it for a monthly report, overkill for a one-off question nobody's going to ask again.

Redshift Spectrum lets you query data sitting in S3 directly, through the same Glue Data Catalog the ETL job already registers its curated table in, without loading a single row into a Redshift table first. A recurring report still deserves the load. A one-off lookup, or heavy repeat joins, point at the right path instead.

This statement creates an external schema named spectrum, pointed at the existing northfield_catalog Glue database — the same catalog the crawler and the ETL job's sink already populate. It reuses northfield-redshift-copy-role, the same role COPY assumes, since Spectrum needs the same kind of S3 read access.

Once that schema exists, querying it looks just like querying any table — region and revenue, scoped to September by a plain WHERE clause on the dt partition. This runs from a Redshift session but never touches fact_orders; it reads the curated Parquet files in S3 directly. The same query works unchanged from Athena, too, since both point at the same catalog table.

So far every load has been triggered by hand, one statement at a time. Next lesson, that stops being true: a scheduled refresh that runs the pipeline every night, with nobody needing to remember to kick it off.
